# Stepper

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

navigation and disclosure · tier 3 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

To show where a reader is in a task of a few steps: a sign-up, a checkout, a setup. It shows; it does not navigate.

```tsx
<Stepper
  aria-label="Sign-up"
  value="details"
  items={[
    { id: 'account', title: 'Account' },
    { id: 'details', title: 'Details' },
    { id: 'review', title: 'Review' },
  ]}
/>
```

- **A step** is `{ id, title, status? }`: `id` a string, `title` any node, `status` one of `done`, `current`, `todo`, `error`.
- **`value`** is the id of the current step. Steps before it are done (a tick), steps after it todo (a number on a line). With no `value` the first step is current; a `value` no step has leaves every step todo.
- **`status`** on a step wins over `value`: `error` draws an x and is read as "Needs attention".
- **Server first.** `items` is plain data and nothing here runs in the browser, so a server page passes it as it is.
- **Arabic.** `{...getLabels('ar')}` says each status in Arabic with Latin digits; `{...getLabels('ar-u-nu-arab')}` writes the numbers in Arabic-Indic digits. The steps run from the right by themselves.
- **A long title** wraps inside its column and is never cut.
- **How many steps.** Each step gets an equal column, so the circles stay apart while a column is at least one circle wide: about 8 steps at `md` on a 320 px phone. Past that the circles overlap.
- **No steps** renders nothing.

## What the platform gives

| Need | Given by |
|---|---|
| "Step 2 of 4" | the `<ol>`, with `role="list"` written so Safari with VoiceOver keeps it |
| The current step | `aria-current="step"` |
| Done, todo, needs attention | a hidden word after each title, from `labels.stepper` |

The circles are hidden from screen readers: the list gives the number and the word gives the state.

## Not built

Clickable steps, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` (choice 10); a panel per step and next or back buttons; `orientation` (vertical); `compact`; `showConnector`; a description line; a disabled look; `tone`.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Stepper } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `items`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | **yes** | `readonly StepperItem[]` | - | The steps, first to last. A connector runs from each circle to the next. |
| `labels` | no | `Labels` | - | The built-in strings, which say each step's status. Defaults to English; spread `getLabels(locale)` for another. |
| `locale` | no | `string` | - | The locale the step numbers are written in: `ar-u-nu-arab` gives Arabic-Indic digits. Defaults to `en`. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The size of the circles (24 to 48 px) and of the titles; custom emits none. |
| `value` | no | `string` | - | The id of the current step: those before it are done, those after it todo. Defaults to the first step's id. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
